source.title: ParaScopes: Do Language Models Plan the Upcoming Paragraph?

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether information about upcoming paragraph text can be decoded from a single-token residual state, using continuation with transferred activations and trained residual-to-SONAR maps rather than the rhyme-word method in the claim.
record.gate_note: Reports output-similarity and rubric results for residual-state decoding, plus layer and token-position experiments. Hyperparameter sweeps and weight norms are discussed, but not recorded as findings rows because they are used to select or inspect the method rather than directly measure future-text decoding.
record.test_reason: Decodes upcoming-paragraph content from a single transition-token residual state (continuation patching and residual-to-SONAR maps) in Llama-3.2-3B and Gemma-2-9B. This bears directly on V2 by a different method than Future Lens. It also bears on V6 via the token-position result that next-paragraph information appears only at the boundary.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the author says both decoders perform comparable to five tokens of cheat context, well above random but below full-context regeneration. Also add that the \n\n token marks the start, not the only site, of next-paragraph encoding, with little information beforehand.
record.recipe_differences: Paragraph-level residual-state continuation and trained residual-to-SONAR embedding maps, not rhyme-word representations or rhyme-changing interventions. Continuation transfers a transition-token state into a blank context; SONAR ParaScope decodes a learned map from the residual state.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by decoder and evaluation metric: SONAR retains broad subject matter better, while Continuation ParaScope scores better on coherence; topic information is reported to emerge around the newline-newline token and to persist afterward. In the single-pair layer scrub, layers 25–35 and the final layer have greater reported impact than the first 25 layers.

fits_no_version.finding: SONAR ParaScope coherence is low (1.9% mostly coherent) while continuation is coherent (53%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decoder output fluency differs by residual-stream decoding method.

record.problems: The post says the methods work only sometimes and that rubric, cosine-similarity, and other metrics are imperfect. The layer-scrubbing experiment uses one A/B example; token-position results are described as noisy and metric-dependent. The large-scale results focus on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, with Gemma-2-9B-it used in narrower experiments. Rubric results have no reported uncertainty in the text.

untested.parts: Prediction beyond the immediately next paragraph (n+2 is proposed, not run); exact-token prediction at fixed offsets; models beyond Llama-3B/Gemma-9B.
Whether decodable content is explained by local next-token features or heuristics versus a steering plan; the explicit vs implicit steering distinction is discussed, not tested.
No test of features computed for later-position use.
No rhyme mechanism in open models.

missing.what: Neutral baseline (0.08 cosine, 0.192 BLEURT) and regeneration (0.82 cosine, 0.619 BLEURT; 99.0% subject 1+) as rows or as baselines on r1–r6 and r11–r22
missing.locator: Cosine and BLEURT tables; Subject Maintenance

record.verdict_notes: A LessWrong post, not an original source. Several record states used cheat-5 as the reference baseline, understating the effect relative to the neutral control. V6 support rests only on the pre-boundary token-position result and the author's interpretation; it is not a test of local-feature explanations.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse prompts, candidate rhyme words, or interventions to change an ending.
Tests paragraph-level content in generated model text, not arbitrary token prediction tasks or all possible distances ahead.

Does not establish that features are computed specifically because they help later positions rather than as a side effect of next-token prediction; no selective removal of future-use features during ordinary generation.
Does not test the rhyme mechanism in open-weight models using open attribution-graph or probing tools.
No multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or other architectures are tested.

The post distinguishes implicit from explicit steering and says explicit-planning evidence is weak, but does not test whether the results are explained by local next-token features or heuristics, nor compare causal steering against that explanation.

tranche.reason: Continuation patching and residual-to-SONAR maps test future-content decodability through different methods.

source_check.notes: Measures concern paragraph semantics, not exact future-token accuracy; failed decoding does not prove information is absent internally. The source reports cheat-10 subject Score 2+ as 51.3%, despite reporting cheat-5 as 55.3%; the rows faithfully reproduce these values.

statements.correction: Llama cosine: linear SONAR 0.50; MLP SONAR 0.51; cheat-5 0.44; neutral 0.08. Gemma token-position experiment: 20 examples; topic-2 decoding begins at the transition and persists afterward. Layer scrubbing: one prompt pair; large changes at layers 25–35; additional significant change at the final layer.
statements.problem: The layer attribution is generalized beyond its single prompt-pair experiment and omits the final-layer effect.
